method: Read existing page-delimited extracted full text; section-screened every assigned paper and focused on closest technical neighbors. This ledger does not claim every line, formula, figure, appendix, citation, or experiment was verified. No experiments were run.
limits: No PDF visual-layout verification; extracted figures may be imperfect.
Reported measurements are author claims, not independently reproduced results.
An arXiv listing is treated as a preprint unless a venue source or an explicitly marked PDF declaration is available.
Page references are numbered extraction markers, not a claim that every line on all listed screening pages was read.
Novelty search is provisional and cannot prove absence of prior work.

papers.title: Don’t Drop Dropout: Optimizing Layer Sparsity for Efficient LLM Training and Inference
papers.source_filename: 001_2026_Don’t Drop Dropout- Optimizing Layer Sparsity for Efficient LLM Training and Inference.pdf
papers.review_depth: Section screening; selected extracted-text sections, not full-line review
papers.contribution: Joint layer-dropout scheduling and hyperparameter tuning; 2,400 runs from 271M to 8.2B parameters; reports up to 25% training-FLOP reduction and 1.55× inference speed.
papers.evidence_limits: Full pretraining uses substantial Cerebras compute; no fault-resilience evaluation. Aggregate efficiency does not establish dependable graceful degradation.
papers.possible_connection: Layer dropping and depth elasticity alone are not a novel resilience mechanism.

papers.title: CASS: Nvidia to AMD Transpilation with Data, Models, and Benchmark
papers.source_filename: 002_2026_CASS- Nvidia to AMD Transpilation with Data, Models, and Benchmark.pdf
papers.publication_status: ACL 2026 long paper; official ACL Anthology PDF
papers.contribution: Paired CUDA/HIP and SASS/RDNA3 corpus, models and 369-task benchmark for NVIDIA-to-AMD transpilation; 60,694 aligned programs.
papers.evidence_limits: Correctness is relative to the benchmark inputs and supported source/assembly environments, not proof for arbitrary inputs or hardware. Runtime/memory parity claims are task-conditioned.
papers.possible_connection: Hardware portability is closely aligned with Mahmoud; reliability would require a contribution beyond translation and test-suite passing.

papers.title: Beyond Prediction: Tail-Aware Scheduling for LLM Inference
papers.source_filename: 003_2026_Beyond Prediction- Tail-Aware Scheduling for LLM Inference.pdf
papers.publication_status: arXiv; supplied PDF declares ICML 2026, venue not independently verified
papers.contribution: UNIBOOST uses prediction-free priority shaping, lightweight distribution statistics and KV-aware preemption; reports improved P99 completion latency over SRPT.
papers.evidence_limits: Results depend on arrival distributions, scheduler settings and preemption costs; no state-integrity mechanism.
papers.possible_connection: Necessary latency/SLO baseline if adding recovery work to an inference server.

papers.title: C2CServe: Leveraging NVLink-C2C for Elastic Serverless LLM Serving on MIG
papers.source_filename: 004_2026_C2CServe- Leveraging NVLink-C2C for Elastic Serverless LLM Serving on MIG.pdf
papers.publication_status: arXiv preprint; placeholder conference text is not venue verification
papers.contribution: C2CServe streams CPU-resident weights into GH200 MIG instances using hybrid HBM/C2C execution and hierarchical scheduling.
papers.evidence_limits: Specific NVLink-C2C hardware and shared-link contention matter; cold-start benefits do not establish numerical reliability.
papers.possible_connection: Shows why resource placement and data movement must be measured in a recovery system, not treated as free.

papers.title: Cascade: Exploiting SLO-Aware Latency Budget for Fair and High Goodput LLM Inference Serving
papers.source_filename: 005_2026_Cascade- Exploiting SLO-Aware Latency Budget for Fair and High Goodput LLM Inference Serving.pdf
papers.contribution: Cascade allocates SLO-aware latency budgets across queuing, restoring, prefetching, retaining and recomputing KV state.
papers.evidence_limits: Goodput depends on workload and remaining-cost estimates. No proof of cache-content correctness.
papers.possible_connection: Budget-aware recomputation scheduling already exists; recovery scheduling alone would be incremental.

papers.title: Efficient Multi-round LLM Inference over Disaggregated Serving
papers.source_filename: 006_2026_Efficient Multi-round LLM Inference over Disaggregated Serving.pdf
papers.publication_status: arXiv; supplied PDF declares ICML 2026, venue not independently verified
papers.contribution: AMPD routes incremental prefill locally or to a disaggregated prefill pool; combines request reordering and deployment planning.
papers.evidence_limits: Offline planner and workload assumptions limit dynamic generality; no silent-data-corruption treatment.
papers.possible_connection: Reusing multi-turn state and deciding when to recompute are crowded; include routing/transfer costs in later scaling.

papers.title: Geometry-Aware Online Scheduling for LLM Serving: From Theoretical Bound to System Practice
papers.source_filename: 007_2026_Geometry-Aware Online Scheduling for LLM Serving- From Theoretical Bound to System Practice.pdf
papers.contribution: Smallest-Volume-First and one-bit variants use request memory–time geometry; supplies competitive analysis and vLLM implementation.
papers.evidence_limits: Competitive bounds are conditional on the formal workload/information model; single-worker evidence is not distributed reliability evidence.
papers.possible_connection: Useful scheduling theory baseline, not a new state-integrity problem.

papers.title: Large-Scale LLM Inference with Heterogeneous Workloads: Prefill-Decode Contention and Asymptotically Optimal Control
papers.source_filename: 008_2026_Large-Scale LLM Inference with Heterogeneous Workloads- Prefill-Decode Contention and Asymptotically Optimal Control.pdf
papers.review_depth: Section screening of a long paper; not a full mathematical audit
papers.contribution: Fluid/queueing control for heterogeneous prefill/decode contention, revenue and SLI fairness using empirical A100 service rates.
papers.evidence_limits: Large-scale evidence is substantially model/calibrated-simulation based; asymptotic optimality requires stated scaling assumptions.
papers.possible_connection: Recovery work changes queueing load; cannot infer tail guarantees from a per-request repair speedup.

papers.title: MoEless: Efficient MoE LLM Serving via Serverless Computing
papers.source_filename: 009_2026_MoEless- Efficient MoE LLM Serving via Serverless Computing.pdf
papers.contribution: MoEless uses layer-aware expert load prediction and serverless replica placement; reports an eight-GPU prototype.
papers.evidence_limits: Expert-footprint and load-prediction assumptions constrain transferability; not fault tolerance.
papers.possible_connection: Expert replication is not a new reliability thesis without integrity semantics.

papers.title: OpScale: Operator-level Provisioning and Autoscaling for LLM Serving
papers.source_filename: 010_2026_OpScale- Operator-level Provisioning and Autoscaling for LLM Serving.pdf
papers.contribution: Operator-level profiling, provisioning, placement and autoscaling; evaluation includes 40 A100 and 24 GB200 GPUs.
papers.evidence_limits: Large-cluster claims cannot be reproduced on one GPU; profile and communication-cost assumptions are material.
papers.possible_connection: Operator-level resource allocation is prior art; a recovery mechanism needs gains beyond ordinary autoscaling.

papers.title: Prefill/Decode-Aware Evaluation of LLM Inference on Emerging AI Accelerators
papers.source_filename: 011_2026_Prefill-Decode-Aware Evaluation of LLM Inference on Emerging AI Accelerators.pdf
papers.contribution: Separates prefill and decode when comparing Llama-2-7B on A100 and Groq; highlights single-stream latency versus batched throughput.
papers.evidence_limits: One model and platform-specific batching support; no universal accelerator winner follows.
papers.possible_connection: A thesis evaluation must separate TTFT, TPOT, batch throughput and hardware assumptions.

papers.title: Scalable Joint Resource Allocation for SLO-Constrained LLM Inference in Heterogeneous GPU Clouds
papers.source_filename: 012_2026_Scalable Joint Resource Allocation for SLO-Constrained LLM Inference in Heterogeneous GPU Clouds.pdf
papers.contribution: Joint model, GPU, parallelism and routing allocation using MILP and scalable heuristics.
papers.evidence_limits: Near-optimality is relative to a calibrated resource/SLO model and synthetic scenarios; not real-time fault handling.
papers.possible_connection: Avoid repackaging profile-driven resource optimization as reliability.

papers.title: FastKV: Decoupling of Context Reduction and KV Cache Compression for Prefill-Decoding Acceleration
papers.source_filename: 013_2026_FastKV- Decoupling of Context Reduction and KV Cache Compression for Prefill-Decoding Acceleration.pdf
papers.publication_status: ACL 2026 Findings; official ACL Anthology PDF
papers.contribution: FastKV decouples context reduction for prefill from KV compression for decode via token-selective propagation.
papers.evidence_limits: Importance stabilization and aggregate quality are model/task dependent; discarded information is not formally protected.
papers.possible_connection: Selective propagation is an efficiency comparator; approximate token omission must not be labeled exact repair.

papers.title: From Bits to Chips: An LLM-based Hardware-Aware Quantization Agent for Streamlined Deployment of LLMs
papers.source_filename: 014_2026_From Bits to Chips- An LLM-based Hardware-Aware Quantization Agent for Streamlined Deployment of LLMs.pdf
papers.review_depth: Section screening; one extracted figure was not interpretable
papers.contribution: HAQA uses an LLM agent to search hardware-aware quantization/deployment configurations across CNN and language-model examples.
papers.evidence_limits: Mixed experimental settings and hardware-specific tuning; no sound end-to-end quality contract. Figure typography was not visually verified.
papers.possible_connection: An agent wrapper around quantization search is not a sufficient new thesis mechanism.

papers.title: InnerQ: Hardware-Aware Tuning-Free Quantization of KV Cache for Large Language Models
papers.source_filename: 015_2026_InnerQ- Hardware-Aware Tuning-Free Quantization of KV Cache for Large Language Models.pdf
papers.review_depth: Focused main-text review; pp. 2–4 and final references/appendix not fully read
papers.contribution: InnerQ groups the inner GEMV dimension (K per token, V per channel), uses fused dequantization, adaptive symmetric/asymmetric groups, and FP16 sink/recent windows.
papers.evidence_limits: Quality experiments and latency evidence use different settings: simulated quantization on task suites versus batch-one Jetson Xavier NX microkernels. Metadata, zero points and preserved windows must be included in effective bit cost; not an end-to-end server speed claim.
papers.possible_connection: Quantized layout and metadata can affect corruption propagation, but generic KV quantization and kernel fusion are established here.

papers.title: Lossless but Not Free: An Empirical Anatomy of Speculative Decoding on Consumer Hardware
papers.source_filename: 016_2026_Lossless but Not Free- An Empirical Anatomy of Speculative Decoding on Consumer Hardware.pdf
papers.contribution: Studies speculative decoding on consumer Apple hardware; verifier/drafter bottlenecks explain why only some model pairings accelerate.
papers.evidence_limits: Distribution tests and greedy agreement are finite empirical checks, not universal implementation proofs; Metal execution limits are hardware-specific.
papers.possible_connection: Charge verification and recovery overhead; mathematical losslessness does not imply practical speedup.

papers.title: ReCache: Efficient KV Cache Reuse and Compression for Tool-Augmented LLM Agents
papers.source_filename: 017_2026_ReCache- Efficient KV Cache Reuse and Compression for Tool-Augmented LLM Agents.pdf
papers.review_depth: Focused main-text review; p. 2 and appendices not fully read
papers.contribution: ReCache isolates tool/resource attention, resets local positions, trains reusable resource representations, and prunes using leave-one-resource-out invocation loss.
papers.evidence_limits: Requires fine-tuning and changed attention structure. Reported 7.2 versus 26.3 ms TTFT excludes offline cache build; OOD invocation F1 falls relative to the uncompressed model. General dialogue reuse is not established.
papers.possible_connection: Persistent reusable tool KV state is already studied; use as a possible workload, not the novelty claim.

papers.title: The Diminishing Returns of Early-Exit Decoding in Modern LLMs
papers.source_filename: 018_2026_The Diminishing Returns of Early-Exit Decoding in Modern LLMs.pdf
papers.contribution: Benchmarks early-exit adaptability and oracle upper bounds; newer architectures/checkpoints often offer less redundant depth.
papers.evidence_limits: Oracle opportunities are not deployable decision policies, and selected checkpoints do not establish universal trends.
papers.possible_connection: Do not assume a cheap early-exit detector or large spare layer budget.

papers.title: TurboQuant: Online Vector Quantization with Near-optimal Distortion Rate
papers.source_filename: 019_2026_TurboQuant- Online Vector Quantization with Near-optimal Distortion Rate.pdf
papers.publication_status: arXiv first submitted 2025; supplied filename year is not publication verification
papers.review_depth: Section screening; theorem proofs not audited
papers.contribution: TurboQuant combines random rotations, scalar quantization and residual inner-product correction with near-optimal vector-distortion analysis.
papers.evidence_limits: Vector distortion and inner-product properties do not directly imply full-generation or application correctness; metadata and implementation precision matter.
papers.possible_connection: Any KV-risk certificate must distinguish local numerical distortion from trajectory-level correctness.

papers.title: Understanding Efficiency: Quantization, Batching, and Serving Strategies in LLM Energy Use
papers.source_filename: 020_2026_Understanding Efficiency- Quantization, Batching, and Serving Strategies in LLM Energy Use.pdf
papers.contribution: Measures precision, batching and arrival-shaping effects on H100/TGI energy; compute-bound prefill and decode respond differently.
papers.evidence_limits: Large energy ratios include utilization/arrival effects rather than a single algorithmic gain; dequantization can hurt decode.
papers.possible_connection: Measure energy per completed request with latency and load held comparable, not merely kernel FLOPs.

papers.title: Coordinating GPU Data Centers and Power Grid Regulation Service for Exogenous Carbon Benefits
papers.source_filename: 021_2026_Coordinating GPU Data Centers and Power Grid Regulation Service for Exogenous Carbon Benefits.pdf
papers.publication_status: arXiv; supplied PDF declares ICS 2026, venue not independently verified
papers.contribution: EcoCenter coordinates GPU power modulation with grid-frequency regulation and evaluates exogenous carbon benefits.
papers.evidence_limits: Counterfactual grid/reserve assumptions drive carbon claims; not a study of numerical faults or cache recovery.
papers.possible_connection: Peripheral motivation only; no reason to force power-grid objectives into an inference-integrity thesis.

papers.title: DataStates-LLM: Scalable Checkpointing for Transformer Models Using Composable State Providers
papers.source_filename: 022_2026_DataStates-LLM- Scalable Checkpointing for Transformer Models Using Composable State Providers.pdf
papers.contribution: Composable StateProviders separate state abstraction from movement; nonblocking lazy snapshots exploit weight immutability and coalesced staging.
papers.evidence_limits: Checkpoint throughput assumes capture consistency/overlap; experiments up to 70B and 256 A100s do not validate state content or detect SDC.
papers.possible_connection: A strong baseline for checkpoint plumbing; copying an already incorrect state does not make it trustworthy.

papers.title: KernelBench-Verified: Do LLM-Generated Kernels Actually Beat PyTorch?
papers.source_filename: 023_2026_KernelBench-Verified- Do LLM-Generated Kernels Actually Beat PyTorch-.pdf
papers.review_depth: Focused full main-text review; appendices not fully read
papers.contribution: KernelBench-Verified strengthens baseline precision settings, hidden input transformations and memory measurement for seven models on a 250-task-derived suite.
papers.evidence_limits: Fixed shapes remain legitimate specialization; finite transformed inputs and a fixed tolerance do not establish arbitrary-input correctness. Maximum allocation measures space, not memory traffic; no training or cross-GPU compositional guarantee.
papers.possible_connection: Generic hidden-test kernel verification is already occupied; declare the numerical baseline contract and include whole-model costs.

papers.title: LLM-PRISM: Characterizing Silent Data Corruption from Permanent GPU Faults in LLM Training
papers.source_filename: 024_2026_LLM-PRISM- Characterizing Silent Data Corruption from Permanent GPU Faults in LLM Training.pdf
papers.review_depth: Focused main-text review; p. 2 and final pages not fully read
papers.contribution: LLM-PRISM maps permanent GPU fault signatures into structured tensor-level injections and studies full-training trajectories, including silent downstream degradation despite benign perplexity.
papers.evidence_limits: GPT-2-scale models/data and a single-defect activation model limit transfer. Proprietary/raw RTL signature availability was not established; causal datatype explanations should not be generalized beyond measured evidence.
papers.possible_connection: Realistic finite, correlated faults and application-level outcomes are essential for a dependable-inference thesis; random single-bit tests alone are inadequate.

papers.title: PHOENIX: Resilient LLM Training with Hot-Swapping via Zero-Overhead Checkpoint
papers.source_filename: 025_2026_PHOENIX- Resilient LLM Training with Hot-Swapping via Zero-Overhead Checkpoint.pdf
papers.contribution: PHOENIX combines remote-memory checkpoints, hot spares, communicator reconstruction and overlapped checkpointing for rapid training recovery.
papers.evidence_limits: Detected fail-stop failures differ from finite SDC. Zero-overhead claims depend on overlap and reserve-resource accounting.
papers.possible_connection: Generic fast checkpoint/restart is prior art; same checkpoint resources must be given to a recovery baseline.

papers.title: ReCoVer: Resilient LLM Pre-Training System via Fault-Tolerant Collective and Versatile Workload
papers.source_filename: 026_2026_ReCoVer- Resilient LLM Pre-Training System via Fault-Tolerant Collective and Versatile Workload.pdf
papers.contribution: ReCoVer combines fault-tolerant collectives, in-step gradient recovery and workload redistribution over surviving GPUs.
papers.evidence_limits: Gradient/statistical equivalence is not necessarily bit-identical floating-point execution; tested failures are not general undetected corruption.
papers.possible_connection: Failure recovery needs a precise correctness target and explicitly scoped fault model.

papers.title: The Anatomy of Silent Data Corruption: GPU Error Pattern Study and Modeling Guidance
papers.source_filename: 027_2026_The Anatomy of Silent Data Corruption- GPU Error Pattern Study and Modeling Guidance.pdf
papers.contribution: Gate-level study of a reduced production GPU yields structured finite SDC patterns: many multibit corruptions, nullification, unit-dependent bit positions and warp periodicity.
papers.evidence_limits: Single stuck-at gate faults, selected microbenchmarks and conditioning on corruption events are not field failure rates. The unnamed reduced GPU and protected memory hierarchy constrain extrapolation.
papers.possible_connection: Use published structured fault families as clearly labeled models; do not call synthetic tensor perturbations physically faithful without validated mapping.

papers.title: The Correctness Illusion in LLM-Generated GPU Kernels
papers.source_filename: 028_2026_The Correctness Illusion in LLM-Generated GPU Kernels.pdf
papers.review_depth: Focused full main-text review; references/appendix not fully read
papers.contribution: Schema-driven operator testing uses boundary shapes, high-precision references, per-operator/dtype tolerances and replay across five GPUs.
papers.evidence_limits: Many errors are seeded and some tests use stand-ins; this is not a measured natural error prevalence for all generated kernels. Finite tests and cross-hardware agreement are not proofs.
papers.possible_connection: An improved generated-kernel fuzzer alone would be a weak novelty claim.

papers.title: Training LLMs with Fault Tolerant HSDP on 100,000 GPUs
papers.source_filename: 029_2026_Training LLMs with Fault Tolerant HSDP on 100,000 GPUs.pdf
papers.contribution: Fault-tolerant HSDP uses data-replica failure units, dynamic membership and nonblocking recovery/catch-up at reported 100,000-GPU scale.
papers.evidence_limits: Scale and failure rates are deployment-specific; smaller-scale accuracy evidence and detected failure handling do not establish SDC protection.
papers.possible_connection: Useful context for major fault-tolerance problems, not a feasible first experimental system for one GPU.

papers.title: V-ABFT: Variance-Based Adaptive Threshold for Fault-Tolerant Matrix Multiplication in Mixed-Precision Deep Learning
papers.source_filename: 030_2026_V-ABFT- Variance-Based Adaptive Threshold for Fault-Tolerant Matrix Multiplication in Mixed-Precision Deep Learning.pdf
papers.contribution: V-ABFT models checksum-difference variance directly, calibrates hardware error, and computes checksums before low-precision output rounding to improve mixed-precision fault detection.
papers.evidence_limits: Practical thresholds use independence/approximately Gaussian assumptions, a 2.5-sigma multiplier and empirical hardware calibration. Zero observed false positives is not distribution-free soundness. Low-bit faults remain difficult; exact correction assumes at most one error per row.
papers.possible_connection: Mandatory producer-boundary baseline for compute-origin KV errors. A tighter threshold or ordinary ABFT wrapper is not sufficient novelty.

papers.title: Beyond Linear Probes: Dynamic Safety Monitoring for Language Models
papers.source_filename: 031_2026_Beyond Linear Probes- Dynamic Safety Monitoring for Language Models.pdf
papers.publication_status: Supplied PDF states ICLR 2026; external venue independently unverified
papers.contribution: TPC dynamically evaluates progressively higher-order polynomial activation probes, with early exits for easy cases.
papers.evidence_limits: Harmful-prompt classification is not response or hardware-error monitoring; finite benchmark evidence does not settle shifted/rare-positive generalization.
papers.possible_connection: Adaptive semantic probes already exist, and should not be presented as reliable hardware integrity witnesses without validation.

papers.title: Online Safety Monitoring for LLMs
papers.source_filename: 032_2026_Online Safety Monitoring for LLMs.pdf
papers.publication_status: Supplied PDF states ICML 2026 Hypothesis Testing workshop
papers.contribution: Online threshold monitoring with calibrated external verification signals; compares simple constant thresholds with sequential alternatives.
papers.evidence_limits: Calibration and signal quality are essential; token likelihood can be weak, and expensive external verifiers must be charged. Workshop status is not a main-conference acceptance.
papers.possible_connection: A risk monitor or threshold gate alone is a crowded direction; hardware recovery needs a distinct mechanism.

papers.title: Preserving Fairness and Safety in Quantized LLMs Through Critical Weight Protection
papers.source_filename: 033_2026_Preserving Fairness and Safety in Quantized LLMs Through Critical Weight Protection.pdf
papers.contribution: Protects critical weights at higher precision using contrastive/gradient sensitivity, studying multilingual fairness and safety under quantization.
papers.evidence_limits: Weight-focused, finite benchmark and judge-based evaluation; runtime hardware cost and broad distribution-shift protection need separate evidence.
papers.possible_connection: Critical-weight precision protection is prior art; a KV-state study must show a fundamentally different persistent-state problem.

papers.title: ProbGuard: Calibrated Safety Risk Estimation from LLM Output Distributions
papers.source_filename: 034_2026_ProbGuard- Calibrated Safety Risk Estimation from LLM Output Distributions.pdf
papers.contribution: ProbGuard estimates calibrated risk from probability-weighted early-token representations and Monte Carlo continuation labels.
papers.evidence_limits: Offline labeling can be costly; finite prefix calibration does not imply universal shift robustness. No hardware-fault or state-repair semantics.
papers.possible_connection: A calibrated early warning wrapper is not the desired dependable-systems thesis.
